title: Multi-Digit Addition & Subtraction Word Problems
intro: Teach large-number word problems by separating the situation from the arithmetic.
html:
Teaching notes for parents and teachers

How to teach it

Sketch the warehouse's starting cable supply and the amount received or shipped. After choosing an equation, model place-value alignment.

Example to work through together

Use the model below as you explain the example. Have your student point to the quantities as you discuss them.

Stored: 248,650 feet. Received: 175,480 feet.

248,650 + 175,480 = 424,130

The warehouse now has 424,130 feet of cable.

500,000 − 176,450 = 323,550

Check: 323,550 + 176,450 = 500,000.

Ask your student

Does the answer describe cable received, cable shipped, or cable remaining?

If your student needs help

If the student gets lost in the digits, use a smaller example of the same situation before returning to the problem.
